memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Anyone the man with a discharge touches without rinsing his hands with water must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.'" - Lev 15:11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice the small mercy tucked into this verse: without rinsing his hands. If the man had washed, the contact did not transfer.

He was not helpless. There was something he could do — a simple act of care that protected everyone around him. A basin of water and a moment's thought, and his family could be spared.

That is a dignity worth noticing. God did not leave this man as purely a source of trouble to others. He gave him a way to take responsibility, to love his household practically in the middle of his own affliction.

Many people in hard circumstances long for exactly this — not to be only a recipient. The person who is ill still wants to give something. The one who is struggling financially still wants to contribute. To be always on the receiving end is its own weight.

Whatever your limitation, there is almost always something. A word of encouragement. A prayer for someone else. A phone call. A washed pair of hands.

Jesus washed feet on the night before He died (John 13:14-15). Small water, small basin, small task — and it has echoed for two thousand years. God does not measure service by scale.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you feel you have nothing to give in your current circumstances?
2. What small act of care is actually within your reach today?
3. Who has served you in a small way that meant a great deal?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You give even the struggling something to offer. Show me the small act of care within my reach today, and let me serve others there. Amen.
